test_criteria.trigger: Confirmed orders for a named accelerator require more advanced packaging capacity than is available by its shipment deadline.
test_criteria.observable: Units shipped or delivery dates for that accelerator against the designer’s original shipment plan.
test_criteria.window: The shipment quarter covered by the original plan.
test_criteria.supports_if: The designer or its supplier attributes a shipment shortfall or delay against the plan to unavailable packaging capacity.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: The packaging constraint is documented, yet the designer delivers the full planned quantity on time, for example by securing alternative packaging capacity.

test_criteria.trigger: Automotive or industrial customers cut orders for a named mature process node to draw down inventories.
test_criteria.observable: Quarterly utilisation of the affected foundry capacity compared with the quarter before the order cuts.
test_criteria.window: The quarter of the cuts and the following quarter.
test_criteria.supports_if: Utilisation falls and the foundry attributes the decline at least in part to those order cuts.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: The cuts occur, but utilisation holds or rises through the window and the foundry reports no utilisation loss from the cuts, for example because replacement orders filled the capacity.

Chip tariffs and subsidies change cost and where capacity is built across the sector
China is both a major end market and the target of restrictions, so policy shifts move sector revenue expectations
Revenue is mostly in US dollars and costs in Taiwan dollars, and the ADR is priced off the Taiwan line, so TWD moves change margins and the ADR premium
Taiwan power, water and overseas-investment policy apply to it directly, and cross-strait risk is priced into it first
US subsidy terms and tariff treatment of Taiwan-made chips change the cost of its US build-out
US export controls administered by BIS may restrict which customers in China TSMC can supply and which chips it can manufacture for them.

candidates.relevance: VIX over VIX3M: near-term implied volatility against three-month. Linked from Risk Appetite: Was the volatility term structure signalling market-wide stress when the sector moved?
The 20-session change in the 10-year real yield, ranked against its own previous 250 values. Linked from Yields: Is the sector's move in line with a market-wide repricing from real yields?

The subject's own close against its 200-session average. A description of price standing in for trend-following flows; it measures no one's positioning. Linked from Risk Appetite: Had index trends broken in a way that could trigger systematic selling?

Year-on-year change in monthly revenue as the release states it. A company total standing in for wafer demand; it cannot show whose orders produced it. Origin: Designer guidance and purchase commitments lead foundry wafer demand.
candidates.missing: The value tsmc:monthly_revenue:2026-10 reports for 2026-10-31 was not available before the decision time. An earlier period's value is not used in its place.

evidence.summary: Consolidated revenue for September 2026 was approximately NT$511.86 billion, a decrease of 0.6 percent from August 2026 and an increase of 54.6 percent from September 2025. A reading of the observable; it takes no side on any lead.

citation.locator: Body of the press release, first paragraph

evidence.summary: TSMC's monthly revenue releases give one consolidated total. They have no split by customer, platform or technology node; this was already so in the September 2026 release and earlier ones.
evidence.missing: Monthly revenue or wafer orders by customer or by platform, dated no later than the monthly release.
